questions.question: Describe, step by step, how personal data moves through this process: collection, use, storage, sharing and deletion.
questions.guidance: Go deeper than the ROPA description by covering each stage of the data lifecycle, e.g. 1. Applicant submits online form > 2. Data saved in the case management system > 3. Team verifies the details > 4. Data shared with a service provider where needed > 5. Record deleted at the end of the retention period. Attach a data flow diagram if available.

questions.question: Does the process involve any of the following? List all that apply.
questions.guidance: Options: New technology or AI; Automated decisions about people; Systematic monitoring of individuals (e.g. video surveillance, tracking, location); Profiling; Children or vulnerable individuals; Combining data from different sources; None.
options: Systematic monitoring of individuals (e.g. video surveillance, tracking, location)

questions.question: What is the specific purpose of this processing? What business outcome does it achieve?
questions.guidance: Be specific. 'Improve services' is too vague; 'Verify an applicant's identity before issuing a permit or service' is clear.

questions.question: Will the data be used for any other purpose, now or planned in the future?
questions.guidance: Examples: performance monitoring, analytics, marketing. If Yes, describe in the details column.

questions.question: For each personal and sensitive data item listed in ROPA, why is it needed? Could any item be removed, anonymized or pseudonymized?
questions.guidance: If you cannot explain why a data item is needed, it should probably not be collected.

questions.question: Is this processing necessary to achieve the purpose? Could the same result be achieved with less data or a less intrusive method?
questions.guidance: Describe any alternatives you considered and why they were rejected.

questions.question: Would the individuals reasonably expect their data to be used in this way?
questions.guidance: Consider what they were told and their relationship with the organization. Explain your answer in the details column.

questions.question: Could this processing negatively affect individuals?
questions.guidance: Examples: discrimination, financial loss, damage to reputation, loss of access to a service, distress. If Yes, describe.

questions.question: Why does the legal basis recorded in ROPA apply to this processing?
questions.guidance: Name the specific law, contract, obligation or consent mechanism that supports it.

questions.question: If Consent is the legal basis: how is consent obtained, recorded and withdrawn?
questions.guidance: Attach the consent wording. Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it. Write N/A if consent is not used.

questions.question: If sensitive data is processed: what additional justification or safeguard applies to it?
questions.guidance: Write N/A if ROPA lists no sensitive data.

questions.question: How and when are individuals informed that their data is being processed?
questions.guidance: Examples: privacy notice, signage, form wording, contract clause, email. Attach a copy.

questions.question: Does the notice explain the purpose, data collected, who it is shared with, how long it is kept, and how to exercise rights?
questions.guidance: If Partly, list what is missing.

questions.question: How do you make sure the data is accurate and kept up to date?
questions.guidance: Examples: validation at entry, periodic review, sync with source system.

questions.question: Can individuals ask for their data to be corrected?
questions.guidance: If Yes, describe how.

questions.question: How is the data deleted or anonymized at the end of the retention period recorded in ROPA, and who is responsible?
questions.guidance: State whether deletion is automatic or manual, and how it is evidenced.

questions.question: For each system listed in ROPA, is it hosted on-premise or in the cloud, and in which country?
questions.guidance: List each system with its hosting type and country.

questions.question: Who has access to the data, and how is access controlled?
questions.guidance: Approximate number of users, roles, approval process, and how often access is reviewed.

questions.question: Which technical security measures are in place?
questions.guidance: Options: Encryption at rest; Encryption in transit; Multi-factor authentication; Role-based access; Access logging/monitoring; Backup; Data masking; Other. Confirms in detail the general measures recorded in ROPA.
options: Other. Confirms in detail the general measures recorded in ROPA

questions.question: Which organizational security measures are in place?
questions.guidance: Options: Policies/procedures; Staff privacy training; Confidentiality agreements; Periodic access review; Other.

questions.question: Has there been any security incident or data breach involving this process in the last 24 months?
questions.guidance: If Yes, describe briefly.

questions.question: Is there a signed data processing or data sharing agreement with each external entity listed in ROPA?
questions.guidance: Attach the agreements. Write N/A in details if ROPA lists no external entities.

questions.question: Apart from the transfers listed in ROPA, is the data stored, backed up or accessible outside the UAE?
questions.guidance: Examples: cloud hosting or backups abroad, remote access by overseas support teams. If Yes, list the countries.

questions.question: If an individual asks, can you give them a copy of their data (right of access)?
Can you correct an individual's data on request (rectification)?
Can you delete an individual's data on request (erasure)?
questions.guidance: If legal retention prevents deletion, explain.

questions.question: Can you restrict or stop processing of an individual's data on request (restriction / objection)?
Can you export an individual's data in a common format (portability)?
Are any decisions about individuals made automatically without human review?
questions.guidance: If Yes, describe the decision and any human review step.

questions.question: I confirm the answers are complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge.
questions.guidance: Enter your name and date in the details column.

principles.description: Organization must have a lawful basis in place for processing and disclosing of Personal Data.
Organization must be transparent, open and clear towards Data Subjects when Processing Personal Data.
Organization must process Personal Data only in ways that Data Subject would reasonably expect.
Organization must only collect and process the minimum amount of Personal Data that is relevant, necessary, and adequate to fulfill the purposes for which it is processed.

Organization must only store/ process Personal Data for a specified time period, necessary for the purposes for which the Personal Data has been collected, unless Processing (storing) for a longer time is required by the applicable laws.

Organization must have in place appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure security of Personal Data. Such measures shall protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of Personal Data.
Organization must have appropriate measures and records in place to be able to demonstrate compliance with the PDPL.

Organization must ensure handling/responding the following rights:
- Right to Information Right to Rectification and Erasure  
- Right to Restrict Processing 
- Right to Data Portability 
- Right to Stop Processing / Objection 
- Rights in Relation to Automated Decisions 
- Right to Lodge a Complaint

principles.principle: Third Party and Cross Border Transfer
principles.description:
Organization must ensure the following measures in place:
Organization enters into Data Processing Agreements
If Organization transfers personal data outside UAE, transfer impact assessment is conducted and appropriate safeguards for lawful cross border data transfer are in place
